crime: {WITCH_NAME} grew up in a small communal foster home above a neighborhood billiard room. The residents played pool together when the room closed for the night and followed the same household routines, giving her a secure place among them. When the building was sold, the foster program closed and the residents were placed in separate homes. Every home she entered afterward called her stay temporary.

In prison, an organizer formed an informal three-person pool group with her and a third player. The same three played after dinner on most evenings. The organizer had reliable opponents and help setting up and clearing the table, while the third player had a regular game with practiced opponents. She had a set place as one of the three regulars, and the game became the last step in her daily routine. She made her bunk before washing, washed before breakfast, ate dinner, then went to the recreation room and racked the balls normally before the others were ready.

One evening, with the third player present, the organizer said the fixed trio had only been a teaching arrangement. The organizer had promised the table to other partners for the next evening, and the players would rotate in future games. The third player confirmed the prior agreement. She asked the organizer to keep the same trio, but the organizer refused.

During their final game, the rack held a full triangle of balls. {WITCH_NAME} pointed to a ball at a rear corner, claimed it was chipped, and touched it while it was still in the rack. The organizer removed the supposedly damaged ball so it would not affect play and handed it to her. She placed it on the side rail next to the vacant corner of the triangle. As the organizer finished setting up, the third player turned toward the cue holder on the wall. She said a sharp fragment from the chip might have fallen into the empty corner and could damage the felt. The organizer leaned low across the table to find and remove it.

The third player heard a sharp impact while her back was turned and looked around at once. The organizer had collapsed against the table edge, dead from a crushing blow to the temple that had not broken the skin. {WITCH_NAME} stood away from both the organizer and the table. The triangle was full again, and the ball was no longer on the rail. It looked as though the organizer had struck the table edge while crouching.

The ball in the rear corner had no chip, and a lock of the organizer's hair was caught between it and the neighboring ball. The ball matched the size of the crushed area at the organizer's temple, and the wound and trapped hair lined up with the ball's former position on the rail. Together, the evidence showed that {WITCH_NAME} had summoned the ball from the rail. Her magic drove it straight through the organizer's temple, killing the organizer, and did not stop it until it reached the exact place in the rack where she had bound it.
fields.epitaph: The daybook lies closed on a completed day, and the list of names on its cover omits hers.
execution: An enormous daybook opens on the execution stand, its hard covers enclosing a thick stack of pages. Restraints hold her across the open first spread with the central binding beneath her. The pages and covers exceed what she can lift unaided, so her magic cannot bind them.

Each new page shows another step of her daily routine left unfinished: her bunk unmade, washing skipped, breakfast untouched, her evening meal unfinished, and the pool table unracked. One page starts to settle over her, but another sweeps across before it can lie flat. The rest follow together in a single uncontrolled block.
The page edges strike her shoulders and arms. The weight of the pages forces her chest and hips down against the central binding.
Driven by the machine, the final cover slams shut and crushes her ribs and skull between the cover and the mass of pages. She dies before the book stops moving.

magic.name: Fixed-Place Summoning
magic.text: She can bind an object to a place and later summon it back there.
